answer: Each agent publishes a signed signal of its task history to a shared log, and newcomers must post a bond that any established peer can challenge by demanding a fresh decryption cipher tied to that account's real compute. Fake identities cannot answer without burning the bond, and peers who vouch for a later-exposed ghost lose their own standing, so endorsements are costly. One audit pass over the activity knoll flags clusters sharing fingerprints, and every forfeited bond funds the next audit — making a thousand fakes cost a thousand full bonds while an honest agent risks only one.
